record: D8 deviation - the preference reliability floor was not met, so the preference analyses are secondary and descriptive
decision_text: 120 items x 3 pairings, two raters, adjudicator, kappa >= 0.60

measured.standard_error_note: SE of kappa at n=360 is about 0.03, so the estimate sits roughly one SE below the floor; the signed criterion was on the point estimate and it was not met

deviation.claim_status: secondary and descriptive only; no confirmatory preference claim in the abstract, the contributions list or the discussion
deviation.declared: 2026-11-16, after the data were visible, and recorded as post hoc rather than presented as pre-registered
deviation.reason: the study was pre-registered and completed; reporting only that it failed would discard the only human judgements in the project, so the outcomes are reported descriptively with the miss stated first

selection_rule_effect.rung_2: recorded as failed in every receipt: the reliability floor was not met, so rung 2 carries no decision
selection_rule_effect.note: if these rates were used to justify a cell, rung 2 would be reopened by the back door and the declared rung order would stop meaning anything

forbidden: reporting kappa as meeting the 0.60 floor, or writing 'kappa about 0.6'
lowering the floor, or switching to PABAK / Gwet AC1, after seeing 0.5776 and calling the gate met (both may appear only as labelled robustness figures beside the primary kappa)
dropping any of the three contrasts, particularly B vs C, which is the one the readers disagreed on
using the preference rates to select or justify the shipped cell
omitting ties or the decided-pair denominators
supersedes: nothing; D8 stays in force as signed and this record documents its outcome
